> 知者不言，言者不知。塞其兌，閉其門，挫其銳，解其紛.

Chapter 55 held up a specimen: an infant who has not grown up. Chapter 56 describes the adult — what he looks like after having grown.

Four characters in it, and every one of them is a physical object.

## 知 has a mouth and an arrow in it

知: 詞也, from 口 and 矢. A mouth and an arrow in a single character.

Which makes the opening line quietly ironic: 知者不言, 言者不知 — written in a character that contains a mouth and a projectile.

The chapter is using the word for knowing to say that knowing does not come out as speech. Not because speech is forbidden, but because the thing being pointed at cannot be hit by an arrow.

## 銳 is the awn of a grain

銳: 芒也 — the fine point at the tip of a grass or grain stalk.

挫其銳 — file off that point. Not "curb your temper": remove the fine tip, the place where the thing protrudes and catches.

## 紛 is a horse-tail wrap

紛: 馬尾韜也 — the sleeve that binds a horse's tail. A wrap, a binding, the thing that holds a mass of strands together.

解其紛 — untie that wrap. Not "resolve disputes": unbind the bundle that has been tied up.

## 塵 is dust raised by a deer

塵: 鹿行揚土也 — the earth lifted as a deer runs through.

同其塵 — become the same as that dust. Which is not "humble yourself to the vulgar." It is: be indistinguishable from what is lifted and settles.

## 玄同

> 塞其兌，閉其門，挫其銳，解其紛，和其光，同其塵，是謂玄同.

Six operations, and the result is 玄同 — the dark sameness.

玄 is the depth that does not show. 同 is not agreement, not identity: it is the state in which the distinctions that would produce 親/疏, 利/害, 貴/賤 are no longer generated.

Note that chapter 52 gave the first two of these — 塞其兌，閉其門 — and this chapter continues the list. The same instruction, extended from one character (the mouth) to the whole surface: the point, the bundle, the light, the dust.

## 不可得而親，不可得而疏

> 故不可得而親，不可得而疏；不可得而利，不可得而害；不可得而貴，不可得而賤.

Six 不可得. The repeated phrase is the key: it is not that he refuses these relations, it is that there is no handle by which to establish them.

To be made close, someone must be able to grip you. To be made distant, someone must be able to push you away. Neither is available.

## 故為天下貴

Therefore he is honored by the world.

The line is not a compensation for the loss of relations. It is the consequence: the person with no handle is the one whose position cannot be moved, and what cannot be moved is what others can rely on.

## The two chapters

55: the infant holds inward, and nothing can bite him.
56: the adult has filed the point and untied the bundle, and nothing can attach to him.

Same result by two different routes — one by not having developed, one by having removed what developed.

## A test

Name the three things about you that people use to get close or to push away — a tone, a specialty, a story about yourself. Each is a 銳. The chapter's claim is that filing them off does not make you unreachable; it makes the reach unforced.
